definitions.explanation: All things or affairs without exception. Often used in set phrases and proverbs.

examples.english: All is lost. / It's all over.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}に{任|まか}せれば{万事|ばんじ}{解決|かいけつ}すると{思|おも}っていたが、そうはいかなかった。
examples.english: I thought that leaving it to him would solve everything, but that didn't happen.

notes: A literary word often found in set expressions. The most well-known phrase is {万事|ばんじ}{休|きゅう}す (all is lost, it's all over), from a Chinese historical anecdote. Other common expressions: {万事|ばんじ}うまくいく (everything goes smoothly), {万事|ばんじ}{順調|じゅんちょう} (all is going well), and {万事|ばんじ}に{通|つう}じる (to be well-versed in all matters). Literally means "ten thousand matters."
